summary: This lecture tells of the Quraysh boycott of Banu Hashim and Banu Abd al-Muttalib after Hamzah and Umar embraced Islam. Abu Jahal drew up a pact forbidding trade, marriage and dealings, and hung it in the Kaaba. The Muslims and Abu Talib were besieged in Shi'b Abi Talib for nearly five years until they ate leaves and twigs, while Hakim ibn Hizam and Mut'im ibn Adi smuggled in food. A small group of non-Muslim Quraysh, starting with Hisham ibn Amr, gathered support and stood up against Abu Jahal at Dar al-Nadwa. The Prophet SAW told Abu Talib that termites had eaten the pact except the name of Allah, which proved true and the boycott ended. The ustaz links it to Gaza, recalls that the Prophet SAW honoured Mut'im though he was not Muslim, and warns that the year of sorrow follows.
keyPoints: Abu Jahal decreed a total boycott of Banu Hashim and Banu Abd al-Muttalib, including Abu Talib who was not Muslim.
The boycott pact was written and hung in the Kaaba, and the Muslims were besieged in Shi'b Abi Talib for nearly five years.
Hakim ibn Hizam and Mut'im ibn Adi, not Muslim at the time, sent food in secret.
A small group of ordinary people built the opposition until many stood against the pact before Abu Jahal.
The pact was eaten by termites except the name of Allah, as the Prophet SAW was told, and the boycott ended.

chapters.title: Mut'im stands up to Abu Jahal and a recap
chapters.summary: The lecture opens with Mut'im ibn Adi standing to reject the pact, then recalls Hamzah and Umar and the failure of Amr ibn al-As in Abyssinia.

chapters.title: Abu Jahal decides on a boycott
chapters.summary: Abu Jahal held a meeting and decided on a total boycott of the Muslims, thought of in terms of clans.

chapters.title: Shi'b Abi Talib
chapters.summary: Banu Hashim and Banu Abd al-Muttalib, including the non-Muslim Abu Talib, were confined to Abu Talib's valley and could not leave.

chapters.title: The pact's terms and inflated prices
chapters.summary: The pact banned trade, marriage and speaking. Even when they begged, prices were multiplied.

chapters.title: Hunger in the valley
chapters.summary: Babies cried from hunger and the companions ate twigs and leaves. The ustaz compares this with Gaza.

chapters.title: Hakim ibn Hizam smuggles food
chapters.summary: Hakim, Khadijah's nephew, released a camel laden with grain at night despite the Quraysh patrols.

chapters.title: Khadijah and Mut'im ibn Adi
chapters.summary: Khadijah shared the food first with mothers and the hungry. Mut'im ibn Adi also sent food and fought the patrols.

chapters.title: Year after year and the pact is hung
chapters.summary: Khadijah fell ill and the Prophet SAW was guarded each night. The pact was written on hide and hung in the Kaaba.

chapters.title: The small group that opposed it
chapters.summary: Hisham ibn Amr persuaded Zuhair, Abu'l-Bukhtari and others one by one until there were enough.

chapters.title: Life in the camp
chapters.summary: The ustaz compares the valley with refugee camps: dirty water, no toilets, heat, cold and hunger.

chapters.title: Standing up at Dar al-Nadwa
chapters.summary: Zuhair rose first, then Mut'im and others, until many said they never agreed to the pact. The ustaz links it to a UN walk-out.

chapters.title: The termites and Abu Talib's wager
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW told Abu Talib the pact was eaten by termites except Allah's name. Abu Talib challenged Abu Jahal, offering to hand over the Prophet SAW if untrue.

chapters.title: The pact is opened and the boycott ends
chapters.summary: The pact was brought out and found eaten, and all returned home. The ustaz notes that change begins with small people.

chapters.title: Honouring Mut'im ibn Adi
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW said he would free the Badr captives had Mut'im been alive. The ustaz urges honouring non-Muslims who help and not backing oppression.

chapters.title: Q&A: Abu Lahab and the fate of non-Muslims
chapters.summary: Abu Lahab did not join the siege. The ustaz answers about the fate of Abu Talib, Mut'im and the Prophet's parents, saying Allah decides.

chapters.title: Q&A: Khalid ibn al-Walid
chapters.summary: The ustaz introduces Khalid, son of al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who appears at Uhud, embraces Islam and is called the Sword of Allah, dying on his bed.

people.role: Quraysh chief and leader of the boycott
people.context: Led the meeting that wrote the boycott pact and tried to silence dissent.
Was besieged to protect the Prophet SAW and challenged Abu Jahal to open the pact.
Lived through the siege, fell ill and shared food with the hungry first.

people.role: Khadijah's nephew, born in the Kaaba
people.context: Sent camels laden with food at night; later embraced Islam.
Sent food, fought the patrols and opposed the pact at Dar al-Nadwa.
Persuaded one person after another until a group opposed the boycott.
Stood before Abu Jahal and said the boycott had gone too far.
One of those Hisham ibn Amr persuaded to end the boycott.
The only one who did not join the siege and sided with Abu Jahal.

people.role: Son of al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, later the Sword of Allah
people.context: Still young at this time; would appear at Uhud and embrace Islam.

sirah.era: About the seventh to tenth year of prophethood: the boycott
sirah.summary: This lecture covers the Quraysh boycott, the siege at Shi'b Abi Talib and the cancelling of the pact.

events.label: Boycott
events.title: Quraysh decide on the boycott
events.desc: Banu Hashim and Banu Abd al-Muttalib were isolated and barred from dealings.

events.label: Shi'b
events.title: Besieged in Shi'b Abi Talib
events.desc: They lived in tents, cut off, for nearly five years.

events.label: The pact
events.title: The pact is hung in the Kaaba
events.desc: The terms were written on hide and hung up.

events.label: The group
events.title: The opposition group forms
events.desc: Hisham ibn Amr gathered people one by one.

events.label: Nadwa
events.title: Standing at Dar al-Nadwa
events.desc: Zuhair, Mut'im and many more rejected the pact.

events.label: Termites
events.title: Termites eat the pact
events.desc: The Prophet SAW was told only the name of Allah remained.

events.label: The end
events.title: The boycott ends
events.desc: The pact was opened, proved true, and all returned home.

lessons.title: Change starts with ordinary people
lessons.body: One brave person persuaded another until enough opposed the oppression.

lessons.title: Allah sends help in small ways
lessons.body: Tiny termites were enough to cancel a great pact.

lessons.title: Honour those who help even if not Muslim
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW recalled Mut'im's help though he had died and never embraced Islam.

lessons.title: Do not back oppression
lessons.body: Worse is the Muslim who supports oppression and mocks refugees.

lessons.title: Patience in long hardship
lessons.body: The companions bore hunger and thirst patiently for nearly five years.

lessons.title: The final outcome is left to Allah
lessons.body: We cannot know a person's final state as he may have embraced Islam secretly; Allah is Most Just.

glossary.meaning: A severing of trade, marriage and social ties.
A valley or lane, here the area of Abu Talib.
The assembly hall of the Quraysh leaders before the Kaaba.
The phrase the termites did not eat from the pact.

children.label: Abu Talib's wager
children.detail: Hand over the Prophet SAW if false.
